PRESENT  HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ANIL KUMAR CHOUDHARY By the Court:- Heard the parties.

2. This Criminal Miscellaneous Petition has been filed invoking the jurisdiction of this Court under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 with the prayer to quash the order dated 30.04.2022 passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge-V, Palamau at Daltonganj whereby and where under the learned Additional Sessions Judge has granted Anticipatory Bail to the opposite party No.2 -of whom the petitioner claims to be the wife; in connection with Complaint Case No.181 of 2021 involving the offences punishable (2025:JHHC:38550) under Sections 498A,
494 of the Indian Penal Code of the court of learned S.D.J.M., Palamau.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner has filed an application under Section 125 of Cr.P.C.

It is next submitted that the learned Additional Sessions Judge allowed the anticipatory bail on the ground that the complainant in her statement on solemn affirmation, has not stated about demanding of a car from her.

Learned counsel for the petitioner relies upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Salil Mahajan vs. Avinash Kumar &
Another reported in 2025 INSC 1396 and submits that in that case, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India relied upon its own judgment in the case of Ashok Dhankad vs. State (NCT of Delhi) reported in 2025 SCC OnLine SC 1690 paragraph-19 of which reads as under:-
"19.

(iii) An order granting bail must reflect application of mind and assessment of the relevant factors for grant of bail that have been elucidated by this Court.
[See: Y v. State of Rajasthan (Supra); Jaibunisha v. Meherban9 and Bhag wan Singh v. Dilip Kumar @ Deepu10]

sentences.text: Such grounds must be taken in an application for cancellation of bail; and (vi) An appeal against grant of bail must not be allowed to be used as a retaliatory measure.

Such an appeal must be confined only to the grounds discussed above."
4.
Hence, it is submitted that the prayer, as prayed for in the instant Cr.M.P., be allowed.

5. Learned Spl. P.P. appearing for the State and the learned counsel for the opposite party No.2 on the other hand vehemently oppose the prayer of the petitioner made in the instant Cr.M.P. and submit that the opposite party No.2 never married the petitioner rather the petitioner married the elder brother of the opposite party No.2 namely Pradeep Kumar Paswan.

It is further submitted that as the petitioner was not happy with her husband and she was having illicit relationship with one Chanda Devi vs The State Of Jharkhand on 22 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157584020/
2 boy namely Pahalu Paswan and the petitioner fled away with Pahalu Paswan.

entities.text: Chanda Devi vs The State Of Jharkhand
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is then submitted that in this respect, a Sanha was lodged by the father of the petitioner before the Officer-in-Charge of Chainpur Police Station on 11.05.2022.
It is next submitted that the allegation against the opposite party No.2 is false.

It is further submitted that the petitioner earlier filed one complaint which upon being referred to police under Section 156 (3) of Cr.P.C., Chainpur P.S. Case No.60 of 2006 was registered involving the offences punishable under Section 498A, 323, 504 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 3/4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act against the opposite party No.2 and others.
The opposite party No.2 married Kiran Devi on 11.07.2007 and leading a happy conjugal life with her.

It is then submitted that no (2025:JHHC:38550) illegality has been committed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge- V, Palamau at Daltonganj in granting anticipatory bail to the opposite party No.2.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge- V, Palamau at Daltonganj
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Hence, it is submitted that this Cr.M.P., being without any merit, be dismissed.

6. Having heard the rival submissions made at the Bar and after carefully going through the materials available in the record, it is pertinent to mention here that while granting the anticipatory bail to the petitioner, the learned Additional Sessions Judge-V, Palamau at Daltonganj considered that this is the second case instituted by the petitioner.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge-V, Palamau at Daltonganj
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: It also considered that there is nothing in the statement of the complainant or the inquiry witnesses to show that after disposal of the previous case, the opposite party No.2 made any request, demand or dowry demand from the petitioner or subjected her to cruelty due to non-fulfilment of the demand.

The learned Sessions Judge also considered that though there is allegation made in the complaint that the opposite party No.2 demanded a car from the father and the brother of the petitioner but in her statement on solemn affirmation, the petitioner has not stated about the same nor the same has been stated by the brother of the petitioner, who was examined as an inquiry witness and considering the aforesaid fact, the learned Additional Sessions Judge-V, Palamau at Daltonganj gave the privileges of anticipatory bail to the opposite party No.2.
7.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge-V, Palamau at Daltonganj
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
As has been held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Ashok Dhankad vs. State (NCT of Delhi) (supra), in an appeal (2025:JHHC:38550) against grant of bail, the superior Court is to see whether the order granting bail has reflected application of mind and assessment of the relevant factors for grant of bail and if such order suffers from any kind of perversity; illegality;
inconsistency with law; or it has not considered the relevant factors including gravity of the offence and impact of the crime; then it can be set aside but the conduct of the accused subsequent to the grant of bail may not be taken into consideration while considering an appeal against the grant of bail.

entities.text: Ashok Dhankad vs. State (NCT of Delhi)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 8. Now, coming to the facts of the case; there is no allegation against the opposite party No.2 of any possibility of the opposite party No.2 to influence the prosecution witnesses, threatening the family members of the petitioner or fleeing from the justice or creating any impediment in the fair trial of the case.
9. After perusal of the impugned order, this Court do not find any perversity, illegality inconsistency with law in the said order.

The learned Additional Sessions Judge-V, Palamau at Daltonganj has taken into consideration the relevant factors including the gravity of the offence which is punishable under Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code having a maximum sentence of three years.

sentences.text: Under such circumstances, this Court is of the considered view that this is not a fit case where the prayer prayed for by the petitioner in the instant Cr.M.P. is to be acceded to in exercise of the power of this Court under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
11. Accordingly, this Cr.M.P., being without any merit, is dismissed.
